topic: An Elevator Counterweight Balances the Car
creativeBrief:
Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Five voiced scenes of 6s each: contradiction, clue, mechanism, second_reveal, payoff. Target 25-29s. Visible change every 2-3s. Opening frame already moving. Mechanism by ~5s. Reveal in scene 4. Scene 5 ends on the same framing as scene 1 so it loops. Use lockedVoiceover word for word.
YouTube title seed: What Really Lifts an Elevator?
YouTube description seed: Look behind an elevator car sometime. Guess what's moving the other way. #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
The central fact: Traction elevators hang a counterweight on the other end of the ropes, so the motor only moves the imbalance.
The later surprise: The counterweight usually equals the empty car plus about 40-50% of rated load.
The very first frame shows an elevator car rising in a glass-sided shaft. Nothing in the first second gives the answer away.
Hook test: A (statement) = "This elevator motor barely works to lift you."; B (question) = "What really lifts an elevator?".
Fact boundaries: The motor still does the lifting; the counterweight only reduces the work. Applies to traction elevators, not hydraulic ones.

facts.statement: In traction elevators, a counterweight on the opposite side of the hoist ropes balances the car so the motor needs less power.
The counterweight typically weighs the car plus about 40-50% of the rated load.
